records.question: How do I transfer my SEVIS record to another university?
search_queries: How do I transfer my SEVIS record to another university?
records.answer:
To transfer your SEVIS record out of Drexel, you need to be maintaining valid F-1 or J-1 status. Then complete the [F-1/J-1 SEVIS Transfer Out Form](https://forms.office.com/r/camJYvn38Z?origin=lprLink) with the required documents. Do this before you legally begin studies at the new school, per the [Transfer Out page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/transfer). You should also contact an ISSS advisor in good time, as the [maintaining status page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain) advises.

**Key points for F-1 students:**
- You can transfer at the end of your current quarter, upon completing your studies, or during the 60-day grace period after graduation/OPT.
- You'll choose a "transfer release date." The new school issues a new I-20 after that date.
- Your start date at the new school must be within five months of your Drexel program completion date or the first available start date, whichever is sooner.

**For J-1 students:** If you've graduated or are on academic training, you must apply before your DS-2019 expires. Contact ISSS about the process.

**Important:**
- Any Drexel employment authorization (on-campus, CPT, OPT, academic training) ends on the transfer release date.
- To cancel, change the release date, or switch to a different school, notify ISSS before the release date. After that, ISSS can no longer access your SEVIS record.

If you're a J-1 scholar (not a student), your department and you should submit the J-1 Departure or Transfer Out Notification as described on the [J-1 Exchange Visitors page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals/j1-scholars).
